headline: THE SAME AD WAS REMEMBERED BY 41 PERCENT OF VIEWERS IN A LIGHT AD BREAK AND 26 PERCENT IN A HEAVY ONE.  NOBODY CHANGED THE AD
deck: FreeWheel tested 436 people on identical thirty-second spots inside the same streaming programme.  In the comparison that matters, the only thing changed was how many other ads sat beside the spot.  Recall fell by more than a third.  Every conversation you have ever had about why a film underperformed assumed the film was the variable, and inside one ad break it is not.
tldr: FreeWheel and MediaScience tested 436 people and found the identical thirty-second ad was recalled unprompted by 41 percent of viewers in a light ad break and 26 percent in a heavy one, with nothing about the ad changed.  Ask your next streaming seller what the ad load is on the inventory offered, in minutes per half hour, insist on a range rather than a single average, and be willing to pay more for the lighter one.

Automotive television spending fell 15.4 percent in August while household impressions fell 20.2 percent, which by our arithmetic means the cost of a thousand household impressions rose about 6 percent, and NFL preseason took 22 percent of what the category spent.  Divide your own spend by your own impressions month by month for the last year, and if the cost is rising while the budget falls, model what that money buys as production on a channel you own.

YouTube has loosened its advertiser-friendly rules so graphic gaming content in the first eight to fifteen seconds now earns ad revenue, and gaming and scripted content featuring recreational drugs is eligible too, weeks before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November.  Re-run your YouTube exclusion lists and suitability settings against gaming inventory this week and write down whether you want the newly eligible material in or out.

The European Commission's KIDS Act proposal would make platforms switch off recommendation driven by watch time and clicks for every user under 18, and remove existing under-15 accounts within six months of the rules applying, with fines up to 6 percent of worldwide turnover.  Reprocess your last twelve months of European reporting by age band now, so you hold a clean picture of organic reach to under-18s from before the rules land.

Rocket League's qualifier reported hours watched up 46.5 percent on a broadcast that ran 35 minutes longer, while peak concurrent viewers rose 40.5 percent and average concurrent viewers rose 30.9 percent — and the Overwatch World Cup's average was 43 percent of its peak, which is a usable sanity check.  Write average concurrent viewers into your next live sponsorship contract as a reported deliverable alongside peak and the broadcast duration.

At the IAB's first creator sales event the stated blocker on bigger creator budgets was that nobody agrees what a view is or how to price a creator, and one marketer's answer was that creators already function as his production house.  Split your next creator proposal into the cost of making the assets and the cost of the media behind them, and file the first as production rather than asking finance for a new channel.

Michelle Khare generated more than 25 million views on Instagram and TikTok during the shoot, five months before the long-form video came out, and held every frame of the Tom Cruise stunt's airborne footage back until days after the premiere.  Mark exactly one shot on your next owned video as unspendable, and start posting the making-of the week you begin shooting rather than the week you finish.
